name: Microscopic Colitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Microscopic Colitis Group Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Chronic or recurrent non-bloody watery diarrhea
Characteristic histological findings on colonic biopsies
Collagenous type: thickened subepithelial collagen band >= 10 micrometers
Lymphocytic type: increased intraepithelial lymphocytes >= 20 per 100 epithelial cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Chronic watery diarrhea with normal/near-normal colonoscopy and characteristic histological findings. Biopsies must be taken from multiple colonic segments including right colon.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Collagenous and lymphocytic colitis are subtypes. Incomplete microscopic colitis is a recognized variant. Drug-induced forms are increasingly recognized.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically 4-9 watery stools per day; up to 15+ in severe cases

rare.notes: In severe cases with high-volume diarrhea
Particularly in collagenous colitis due to mucosal fragility

laboratory: ESR and CRP may be mildly elevated
Fecal calprotectin may be mildly elevated (usually < 200 mcg/g)
Autoimmune markers: ANA, anti-thyroid antibodies may be positive (autoimmune association)
imaging: Subtle changes may include edema, erythema, or mucosal lacerations
CT colonography is not diagnostic; histology is essential
genetic: Association with HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 (overlap with celiac disease)
other: Colonic biopsies are essential (from right, transverse, and left colon)
Collagenous type: subepithelial collagen band >= 10 micrometers, surface epithelial damage
Lymphocytic type: >= 20 IELs per 100 epithelial cells without thickened collagen band
Drug history important: PPIs, NSAIDs, SSRIs, acarbose commonly implicated

distinguishingFeatures: IBS-D typically does not have nocturnal diarrhea
BAM responds to bile acid sequestrants
BAM has elevated C4 or positive SeHCAT
Celiac disease has duodenal villous atrophy
Note: celiac and MC can coexist

redFlags: Bloody diarrhea (suggests alternative diagnosis such as IBD or ischemic colitis)
Failure to respond to budesonide (consider alternative diagnosis or refractory disease)
Development of colonic mucosal tears during colonoscopy
references: Miehlke S, et al. European guidelines on microscopic colitis: UEG and EMCG statements and recommendations. United European Gastroenterol J. 2021;9(1):13-37.
Nguyen GC, et al. American Gastroenterological Association Institute Guideline on the Medical Management of Microscopic Colitis. Gastroenterology. 2016;150(1):242-246.
Pardi DS. Diagnosis and Management of Microscopic Colitis. Am J Gastroenterol. 2017;112(1):78-85.
